correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructs the actual quandle multiplication from an associative auxiliary group ring; nilpotent augmentation filtration rules out nonzero augmentation-zero idempotents as scheme points. Truncated log/exp is a natural polynomial group isomorphism because p-th powers vanish. Semisimplicity of the order-(p-1) character action gives exactly (p-1)/lcm(2,ord_p(2)) dimensions. Standalone finite-field row-reduction and quandle-product tests verify representative primes, with exhaustive p3 and p5 enumerations. The finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: 2017 general theory of quandle rings and ideal filtrations does not classify modular idempotent schemes. The 2026 idempotent papers address integral/quasi-integral rings and specific cases; integral rigidity cannot dominate modular positive-dimensional family. No stronger covering statement was found in inspected material.

originality.rationale: Exact published-finding corpus matches the prime-three affine line, which is a strict special case (and not claimed novel). Actual semantically targeted searches located no all-odd-prime dimension/order-of-two formula. Relevant primary texts were inspected, including full 2017 foundational quandle-ring text, 2020 modular-adjacent integral work, and the 2026 integral Fourier and augmentation-ideal studies. Their hypotheses and implications do not give the characteristic-equal-to-prime affine scheme in dimensions two and three. This is best-knowledge scientific novelty, not global uniqueness certification.
residual_risks: Uninspected modular quandle algebra studies could have equivalent stronger result.
published-finding corpus is a semantic record search; nonretrieval does not certify mathematical novelty.

value.rationale: Idempotent schemes of quandle algebras are motivated by literature on augmentation ideals and quandle-based invariants. The theorem determines a natural complete geometric invariant over every odd prime and all coefficient fields in the matching characteristic, resolves exact finite-field counts, and exhibits arithmetic dimensional jumps at p17 and p31, not explained by existing integral-rigidity theory or known p3 example.
